preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10) representing the number of test cases.

postconditions.description: The output consists of T test cases, each producing two lines: the first line is the maximum Hamming distance, and the second line is the array B.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == N for line in stdout.splitlines()[2::2])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the second line of output contains exactly N space-separated integers representing array B.

postconditions.expression: all(all(x in A for x in B) for A, B in zip([list(map(int, stdin.splitlines()[2*i+1].split())) for i in range(T)], [list(map(int, stdout.splitlines()[2*i+2].split())) for i in range(T)]))
postconditions.description: Array B is a permutation (shuffling) of array A for each test case.

postconditions.description: The Hamming distance between A and B is maximized for each test case.
